reason: The hypothesis cites no prior evidence whatsoever. All key premises, including the feasibility of texturing tungsten alloys via directional solidification, the relationship between texture and CRSS, and the link to high-temperature plasticity and toughness, are presented without any supporting citations. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific high-temperature behavior of directionally solidified tungsten alloys.
premises: Directional solidification can engineer a predominant crystallographic texture in tungsten alloys.
Aligning high-symmetry slip planes with the loading direction reduces the critical resolved shear stress (CRSS).
Reducing CRSS enhances dislocation mobility at high temperature.
Enhanced dislocation mobility leads to greater plastic strain and toughness at high temperature.
Conventionally cast tungsten alloys have a random texture that serves as a valid baseline.
